Loop condition uc < ue is false for a 1-byte input (uc=1, ue=1), so the loop body never executes and the function returns 1 (success), leaving *ucp pointing out of bounds.
After json_parse_const returns 1, the local uc pointer (which is *ucp) now points 3 bytes past the end of the 1-byte input buffer.
json_skip_space checks uc < ue which is false (uc is past ue), so it returns the out-of-bounds uc unchanged.
The out-of-bounds pointer is stored back to *ucp, propagating the invalid pointer.
Comparison fails because uc (position 4) is not equal to ue (position 1), so execution continues to the vulnerable read.
Dereferences *uc which points 3 bytes past the end of the 1-byte heap buffer, causing a heap-buffer-overflow READ 1.
